title: 2026 Victorian Election Pendulum
key_points: Lists Kew on the Liberal side at a 4.0 percentage-point margin; notes that only a few hundred extra votes for an Independent could threaten Jess Wilson based on the 2022 contest. The article also discusses three-way competition and preference-flow uncertainty.
interpretation_limit: An electoral pendulum is a historical seat baseline, not a current poll or a candidate win probability. The 4.0-point margin is a historical contest measure and does not itself account for current candidate field or campaign dynamics.

title: VIC2026 – Mapping One Nation’s 2025 Federal Result
key_points: Maps One Nation's 2025 federal House vote onto Victorian state electoral districts and discusses the geographic pattern of support.
interpretation_limit: Federal voting patterns are not the same as state election intention. This is a contextual geographic baseline, not a Kew candidate poll or 2026 seat estimate.

title: VIC2026 – Candidate Numbers at Close of Nominations
key_points: Reports 733 lower-house candidates across Victoria, averaging 8.3 per district, and compares the statewide total with 2022.
interpretation_limit: Statewide candidate counts describe ballot complexity, not support or campaign strength. The Kew nominations and ballot order should be taken from the VEC candidate register.
